title: Murf AI Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits, and Costs
summary: Murf AI pricing spans free and paid tiers with different numbers of voices and monthly word limits you can compare across plans.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Murf AI free to use?


Yes, there's a free plan, but treat it as a trial for auditioning voices, not a production tier.


Its limits on generation and exports are tight, and its licence terms are narrower than the paid plans', so test your script there and budget as if you'll leave it.


### Can I use Murf voices commercially on every plan?


No. Commercial rights are a plan-level term, and the entry-level and free tiers are the likeliest to restrict them.


If your output reaches customers, such as a paid course, an ad or a product with synthetic narration, read the licence text for the exact plan before you build.


If a pricing grid only hints at rights, that is not enough. If the answer takes a sales call to extract, price in that friction.


### Does Murf charge extra for API access?


Plan on it being a separate line item. API usage is metered and governed by its own terms, apart from the generation time you use in the studio editor.


**Studio minutes and API minutes are different budgets** , so a plan that looks generous in the editor can look thin once an automation starts calling the API.


Work out the cost per finished minute for the path you'll actually run. Confirm in writing whether the API draws from the plan's allowance or bills on top of it.


### Can I cancel or downgrade a Murf plan mid-term?


You can stop a plan from renewing, and access normally runs to the end of the period you paid for. Refunds for the unused remainder are a different matter and depend on the billing terms at the time of purchase.


Go annual and you commit a year of spend to a volume you may not have measured yet. The discount is real, but that is the risk. **Run a month-to-month plan until your usage settles, then switch if the numbers justify it.**


### Does unused Murf generation time roll over?


Assume it doesn't. Allowances on plans like this usually reset each billing period, so unused minutes are spend that bought nothing.


The practical consequence is that a lumpy workload, with heavy launch months and quiet ones, costs more per finished minute than a steady one on the same plan.


If your volume swings, size the plan to your typical month rather than your peak, and handle spikes another way. Check the plan's terms for any carry-over exception before you rely on either assumption.
